best_season: Summer, inside the Yakama Nation's visitor window for the Bird Creek side (historically about July 1 to October 1, and shorter in some years); earlier in that window holds more snow.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late August through September, while the Yakama Nation opens the Bird Creek side to visitors; earlier holds more snow

July.reason: The headwall carries its best snow, but the reservation side usually stays closed to visitors until late summer.

June.reason: The Tract D area is closed to non-tribal visitors and the Bird Creek road is still snowbound.

August.reason: The Tract D area typically opens late in the month; the 45-degree headwall still holds snow though crevasses below Sunrise Camp open up.

October.reason: The reservation area closes to visitors around October 1, and early storms ice the headwall.

September.reason: The most reliable month inside the visitor window; expect firm snow or ice on the headwall and open crevasses, and plan a long day-use push.

approach: Start from the Bird Creek Road trailhead (~5,700 ft) on the Yakama Reservation side; route-finding across moraines and glacier fields begins around 6,700 ft, reaching Sunrise Camp at 8,300 ft.

access.permit: Yakama Indian Reservation Tract-D tribal-use permit required to start from Bird Creek Meadows.
access.closures: Non-tribal-member season restricted to roughly July 1–October 1; the Mazama Glacier route and Bird Creek Meadows are among the few reservation-side areas open to public recreation.
access.landManager: Yakama Nation (Yakama Indian Reservation, Tract D)

overnight_permit.what: Yakama Nation Tract D recreation permit for the Bird Creek side, plus the Mount Adams Climbing Pass above 7,000 ft on national forest land
overnight_permit.where: Buy the Tract D permit at the fee station where the road enters the reservation; the area is open to non-tribal visitors only in summer, roughly July to September. The Climbing Pass is sold on Recreation.gov.
